verses.text: And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When they began to sing, God moved. Church, Judah did not have to swing a sword that day. The enemy turned on each other. It took the people three days to carry away everything that was left.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: There are battles that are too big for us. God never promised we would not face them. But he can teach us how to stand in them. Seek him first. Tell him the truth, that you do not know what to do. Keep your eyes on him. And sing before you see it. The battle belongs to the Lord.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to 2 Chr 20:1-22 (vv23-25 told in words); Jahaziel's prophecy read by the narrator; 'prosper' (v20) left in the verse and the close says God never promised we would not face battles; 'The Battle Is Not Yours' named only as what choirs sing.

cultural.note: Praise before the victory, preached plainly; 'God is good / all the time'.
